blocks.text: Why clinical research coordinators need better Excel habits

Your day is full of manual data entry. You move patient info from Electronic Health Records to your own tracking logs. A single typo in a study identifier can cause issues later. Using Excel effectively on your Mac means fewer errors and less time spent fixing mistakes.
Essential Mac keyboard shortcuts for research
Stop using your trackpad for every small action. Use these shortcuts to move through your study logs faster. Remember that your Mac uses the Command key where Windows uses Control.

items: Jump to the edge of your data: Command + Arrow keys
Insert a new line inside a cell: Control + Option + Return
AutoSum your columns: Shift + Command + T

blocks.text: Managing study logs with data validation

Data consistency is vital. You should use data validation to limit what people can enter in your cells. This is perfect for study visit status or site IDs. Go to Data > Data Validation to set up dropdown lists. This prevents someone from typing 'Complete' in one row and 'Comp' in another.
How Lazur helps you in Excel

Lazur lives in your Mac notch. It sees your screen when you hold ⌥ ⌘. If you are stuck looking for a specific setting in the Excel ribbon, just ask Lazur where it is. It will draw a circle around the button for you. You do not need to hunt through menus.

Many coordinators keep their data in a format that Excel cannot read easily. Avoid merging cells for headers. This breaks sorting and filtering. Use Center Across Selection instead. Also, never store dates as text. If your dates align to the left, Excel sees them as words, not numbers. This makes calculating visit intervals impossible.
